title: Para cuando llegues, ya habré terminado
titleEn: By the time you arrive, I'll have finished
blurbEn: A tense for what will already be done — and, oddly, for guessing about what has just happened.
body:
—¿A qué hora llegas?

—Sobre las nueve.

—Perfecto. Para cuando llegues, ya habré terminado de cocinar.

Mi hermana vuelve hoy de Sevilla y he decidido preparar algo decente por una vez. Había comprado los ingredientes por la mañana, siguiendo una receta de internet con demasiados pasos.

A las siete he empezado. A las ocho y media todavía estaba cortando cebolla y llorando.

Habré terminado a las nueve. Puede. Quizá.

Lo curioso del futuro perfecto es que también sirve para adivinar el pasado. Si alguien no contesta al teléfono, dices «se habrá dormido». Si llega tarde, «habrá perdido el tren». No sabes nada, pero lo dices con toda la confianza del mundo.

Mi hermana llegó a las nueve y cuarto. Yo no había terminado.

—¿Qué habrá pasado aquí? —dijo, mirando la cocina.

Cenamos fuera.
translationEn:
"What time do you get in?"

"Around nine."

"Perfect. By the time you arrive, I'll have finished cooking."

My sister comes back from Seville today and I've decided to make something decent for once. I had bought the ingredients in the morning, following an internet recipe with too many steps.

At seven I started. At half past eight I was still chopping onion and crying.

I'll have finished by nine. Maybe. Possibly.

The curious thing about the future perfect is that it also serves for guessing about the past. If someone doesn't answer the phone, you say "he'll have fallen asleep". If they're late, "they'll have missed the train". You know nothing, but you say it with all the confidence in the world.

My sister arrived at quarter past nine. I hadn't finished.

"What will have happened here?" she said, looking at the kitchen.

We ate out.

habré.note: The future of 'haber' plus a participle. It says something will already be finished by a point ahead.

se habrá dormido.note: Not about the future at all — a guess about what just happened. Spanish does this constantly.

habrá pasado.note: Same guessing use, here as a rhetorical question: what on earth happened?

phrases.note: 'cuando' + subjunctive from Unit 13, now with the future perfect in the main clause.
